comments.author: @leonaessens4399
comments.text: I am what used to be called a ''Dutch Colonial'', me being the last generation of a family descended from a French sailor who worked for the Dutch East India Company in 1765. I spent three-and-a-half years as a kid in Japanese concentration camps during World War II. My father was a captain in the Dutch East Indian Army,  my grandfather was a doctor married to an Indonesian girl from Kediri. Born in Sumatra, I grew up in Jakarta. My Bahassa today is probably still better than my English. My father sent me to Holland when I was seven or so, but I eventually came back to attend school in Jakarta. I graduated in Jakarta when I was 19 and then joined the Dutch Army for almost nine years. I returned to Indonesia when I left the Army and eventually married an Indonesian girl. No children, and eventually she got tired of my inability to settle anywhere. My family name is French but I have always seen myself as Dutch. I travelled all my life, never stayed long anywhere, making a living as a journalist working in a dozen different countries over the years. Today I still have four passports that I always carry with me although all of them have expired by now! I am nearly 86 years old, too old to return to Indonesia even if they would be willing to let me come back....

replies.author: @PlanetExplorer-DB
replies.text: Thank you for sharing such an extraordinary life story. Your journey through war, Indonesia, the Netherlands, military service, journalism, and many cultures carries an entire era of history. Indonesia clearly remains deeply rooted in your identity despite a lifetime of movement and loss. We are honored that this video brought those memories back to you.
